initiative.title: Public garden gallery
initiative.summary: An opt-in public wall of garden thumbnails that anyone can pan and zoom, opening one garden at the closest zoom, without revealing where anyone lives.
initiative.next_action: Review and merge the gallery PR. Later: back GalleryStore with the server now that accounts exist.

claims.statement: Owners mark a project public to include it; everything is private by default.
The gallery is a zoomed-out wall of garden thumbnails; you pan and zoom in to open one garden.
claims.notes: Narrowed by G18: Best shows the top 10, not hundreds of gardens.

claims.statement: The public view hides the address and the aerial photo.
Hundreds of thumbnails on one canvas, sharper images loaded as you zoom; fallback is a scrolling grid of cards.
Public portfolios for landscape architects and community projects (Fishers) are later possibilities.
No accounts, server database, or public pages exist yet; projects are local JSON files.
The public gallery's purpose is to show the community's top-rated gardens, with the top-rated ones highlighted.
One rough combined ranking from 1-10 stars and total saves picks the best gardens.
Each person has a personal gallery of their own ideas and designs to reference and look back at; newer gardens live there.
The owner chooses whether each garden is public or not.
Saving a garden puts it in the saver's personal gallery, not the public gallery.
The gallery opens in its own tab inside the designer; a toggle switches between your current design and the gallery, each shown on its own rather than side by side.
A separate New gardens tab lets people go through a few new public gardens, give each 1-10 stars, and use a yes/no toggle to save it.
Zooming into one garden shows its full plan (plant layout, plants, configuration, overall landscape) like the designer, but view only, with address and aerial photo still hidden.
To edit someone else's garden, you save it, open it from your personal gallery, and edit your own copy; the original never changes.
If an owner turns Public off, saved copies stay with the people who saved them.
An edited saved copy can be made public; its public view credits the original garden.
Best shows only the top 10 rated gardens, laid out as a podium with #1 largest.
claims.notes: Byron chose only the top 10 over highlighting them on the full wall.

claims.statement: Every rating counts the same, including your own; one person can't push a garden onto Best.

shape.appetite: One gallery inside the existing app: Best, New, Mine tabs, one wall, one view-only garden view, saved copies. No new editor.
shape.problem: People designing a garden want to see, rate, and borrow from the community's best gardens without losing their own design or exposing where anyone lives.
shape.recommended_shape: Design/Gallery toggle; Best wall ranked by a combined stars-and-saves score; New tab for 1-10 stars and save yes/no; view-only garden view reusing PlanView without the edit layer; Mine holds own gardens with a Public switch and saved snapshot copies. Built behind a gallery-store seam against a local generated community before accounts exist.

success_moves.move: Gallery-store seam with a local fake holding ~500 generated gardens
success_moves.risk: Accounts and server database do not exist; the wall UX would wait on them
success_moves.benefit: Judge the wall, rating, and saving now; real accounts plug into the same seam

success_moves.move: Reuse PlanView without overlay for the view-only garden view
success_moves.risk: Building a second renderer or a read-only editor mode
success_moves.benefit: View-only comes almost free and matches the designer exactly

success_moves.move: Publish a sanitized public copy instead of reading the private project
success_moves.risk: A future private field (address, aerial) leaking into public views
success_moves.benefit: Privacy enforced in one place, testable with a unit test

success_moves.risk: Edits or deletions by the owner breaking savers' work
success_moves.benefit: The original never changes; savers never lose their copy

success_moves.move: Grid fallback for Best behind the same data
success_moves.risk: Pan-and-zoom canvas performance at hundreds of thumbnails
success_moves.benefit: S16 failure changes only the Best layout, not New, Mine, or ranking

first_proof.question: Can a pan-and-zoom wall of ~500 real watercolor thumbnails stay smooth and make the best gardens stand out?
first_proof.artifact: Spike S16: generated gardens from the sample lot, thumbnails from the plan painter, sized by a fake score, closest zoom opens a view-only PlanView
first_proof.decision_rule: Smooth and inviting on a normal laptop: keep the wall and build New and Mine on the local store. Stutters or confusing: Best becomes a score-sorted scrolling grid; everything else unchanged.

rabbit_holes: Accounts and hosting bundled into the first proof
Exact ranking formula tuning before real ratings exist
Live sync of saved copies with originals

history.event: Created from the accounts-and-gallery intent after Byron chose the public garden gallery as the gallery viewer.
Three question rounds: top-rated by saves and 1-10 stars, personal gallery, public toggle per garden, gallery as a tab toggled with the current design.
Round 4: combined ranking, New gardens tab, view-only zoom-in, save then edit from the personal gallery.
Byron confirmed saved gardens open as editable copies; shape brief drafted with a local-first gallery-store seam and S16 as first proof.
Byron decided saved copies stay when an owner turns Public off.
Byron decided edited copies can go public with credit to the original; shape has no open choices.
Implementation plan written; Byron asked to start implementing. Status set to active.
Implemented milestones 1-3 locally (uncommitted). m2 and m3 verified; m1 functional, smoothness still to be observed.
S16 decided: wall is smooth, keep it. All three milestones complete locally; not yet committed.
Top 10 tier added to the Best wall: spans for ranks 1-10, badges, clickable Top 10 list; fit leaves room for the list.
Best narrowed to the top 10 only, as a podium (#1 3x3 center, #2-#3 2x2, #4-#10 row). Top 10 side list removed as redundant.

Mock run added: ?demo=1 seeds 'Rising star meadow' (4 ratings) and a demo bar with Simulate 30 neighbors and Reset. Scenario test in store.test.ts. Fixed Best to refresh when you return to it. Walked through in the browser: your 10 makes it rankable (#39), neighbors carry it to #2.
Byron decided ratings stay equally weighted; no extra weight for the viewer's own rating.
Rebased onto main after accounts landed: toggle moved to /plan, gallery storage scoped per account, underlay (aerial photo) marked private in the public-copy allow list.
